solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Strikes a blow*

indicators.note: blow is read as a verb, to blow apart or scatter, so the letters of the words before it are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A punch thrown, with a mysterious footnote mark trailing after it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blow' signals the anagram of STRIKES A. The definition is the printed symbol itself: the star mark that ends the clue, which also links to 23 Down.
explanation.definitionFit: The star-shaped printed mark used for footnotes is called by this name, so the symbol defines itself.

clue.text: Bachelor in Paris, I engaged in deed of lowest kind

indicators.note: engaged in means the pieces are held inside the deed word

parts.note: an act is a deed
je is French for I

explanation.surface: A bachelor in Paris is involved in some contemptible act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Paris' signals French: JE is French for I.
explanation.definitionFit: Wretched, of the meanest or most degraded sort, a synonym of lowest kind.

clue.text: East End thug turned up in northern waste

indicators.note: turned up, in a down entry, means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: in East End London speech a hard nut, a tough guy, drops the h to become 'ard nut

explanation.surface: A Cockney heavy shows up unexpectedly in an Arctic wilderness.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End of London is home to Cockney speech, which drops the h: 'ard nut for hard nut, a tough man.
explanation.definitionFit: Treeless Arctic plain, a barren northern wilderness described here as waste.

clue.text: Starts skipping from me to lover

indicators.note: skipping the starts means each of the three following words loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone skips from one person to the next lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's young hero is a byword for a passionate lover, a named example.

clue.text: Way to the top is ultimately perilous when wearing skirt

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of perilous
the skirt word is wearing, enclosing, the word for when

parts.note: a kilt is a Scottish skirt
if can mean when, as in 'if it rains, stay in'

explanation.surface: The route up a mountain is risky in a skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable device that carries skiers up the slope is a way to the top of a mountain.

clue.text: Still in command after brief panic

indicators.note: after places the command abbreviation following the shortened panic word
brief means cut short, so the last letter of the word for panic goes

parts.note: being in a state means being in a panic
IC is the usual abbreviation for in charge, in command

explanation.surface: Someone stays calm and in control after a moment of alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: Motionless or unmoving is the sense, synonym of still as an adjective.

clue.text: Chunter on about staff

indicators.note: about means the letters of chunter on are moved around

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles on about their employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees, but is a stick; chunter is British for grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer's short club is a type of staff or stick, an example.

clue.text: Minus view on holiday

indicators.note: on, in a down entry, puts the holiday word beneath the view word

parts.note: a take on something is a view of it
away means away on holiday

explanation.surface: A negative opinion about a vacation.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic, to subtract is to take one number from another, so it means minus.

clue.text: Meet Charlie by side of road

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
on can mean by or beside, as in a town on the river
a verge is the grassy edge of a road

explanation.surface: Arrange to meet Charlie at the roadside.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming together at one point is the sense, a synonym for meet.

clue.text: Bodyguard on East Asian boat is post no-one wants

indicators.note: on, in an across entry, puts the armour word after the boat word

parts.note: a junk is a Chinese sailing vessel
mail is armour that guards the body

explanation.surface: A bodyguard aboard a Chinese sailing vessel is unwelcome cargo.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsolicited advertising letters are the post nobody asked for, a descriptive phrase for it.

clue.text: Union reps and relatives eat heartily

parts.note: the TUC, the Trades Union Congress, represents British trade unions
kin means relatives, family

explanation.surface: Trade union representatives and their families enjoy a big meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The TUC is the Trades Union Congress, the British federation of trade unions.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig in and eat with enthusiasm is the colloquial phrasal verb's meaning, an idiom.

clue.text: Pickle, stew or jam

definitions.meaning: a pickle is a difficult or muddled situation
to be in a stew is to be in a state of confusion
a jam is a tight spot, a predicament

explanation.surface: A list of preserved and cooked foods.
explanation.definitionFit: Each means a predicament or muddle, three colloquial words for a confused situation.

clue.text: Char performing aerobics round pole

indicators.note: round means the rearranged letters go around the pole letter
performing aerobics suggests the letters of aerobics are put through their paces and rearranged

parts.note: N stands for the north pole

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady doing a workout around a pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Char' looks like a cleaning lady (British slang), but it is the verb to scorch. 'performing' rearranges AEROBICS, and 'round' wraps that round N.
explanation.definitionFit: To char something is to burn it to carbon, a direct synonym for scorching it black.

clue.text: Pursue Charles I of England

indicators.note: I is the Roman numeral one, so I of means the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: An instruction to go after the Stuart king Charles the First.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charles I' looks like the king, but the numeral I is read as 'first', picking the first letter of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow someone in order to catch them, a plain synonym for pursue.

clue.text: Revise parts of OED itself

indicators.note: parts of means the letters come from a stretch inside the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: Someone updates sections of the Oxford English Dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct or alter text before publication, a synonym of revise.

clue.text: Daddy has three such offspring

parts.note: D stands for daughter, and the word daddy contains the letter D three times

explanation.walkthrough: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter, as in genealogies, and 'Daddy' has three Ds.
explanation.definitionFit: Female children are offspring, and the clue counts them as letters in the word.

clue.text: Person associated with bust and boom in business

parts.note: a bust, the chest, is linked with a woman, referred to by the female pronoun
a boom is a loud noise, a bang

explanation.surface: Someone linked to an economic crash and boom works in commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust and boom' looks like an economic cycle; bust is the chest, suggesting a woman, and boom is a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: As in 'the whole shebang', the word means an affair or matter, an informal synonym for business.

clue.text: Setting out 1 Dec, goes shortest way from A to B

definitions.text: shortest way from A to B

indicators.note: setting out means the letters are laid out again in a new order

parts.note: 1 is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone departs on the first of December and travels the most direct route.
explanation.definitionFit: The shortest line between two points on a curved surface, the mathematical term for it.

clue.text: Fury as fruit tree is split by old axes

indicators.note: split by means the tree word is broken open by the letter for old

parts.note: an apple is a fruit tree
x and y are the axes of a graph

explanation.surface: Rage at an apple tree cut through by ancient axes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'axes' looks like choppers for the tree, but means the X and Y axes of a graph.
explanation.definitionFit: A fit of extreme rage, as in apoplectic with fury, is a figurative sense.

clue.text: Present or former currency

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
the pound is a currency

explanation.surface: A choice between a gift and money that is no longer in use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a noun, a gift, but it is the verb to set out an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: To present an idea is to set it out in detail, a synonym of explain or present.

clue.text: Knights head of dynamic Swiss bank

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the following word

parts.note: UBS is a major Swiss bank

explanation.surface: A bank in Switzerland honours its energetic chief.
explanation.definitionFit: To dub someone is to confer a knighthood by touching the shoulder with a sword.

clue.text: Call round

definitions.meaning: to telephone someone, to give them a call
a circle or band, something round

explanation.definitionFit: It means both to telephone someone and a circular band, two separate senses.

clue.text: What Greens do on bike

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a letter heading
a bike is a cycle

explanation.surface: Environmentalists travel by bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: Greens are environmentalists, members of a Green party.
explanation.definitionFit: Environmentalists reuse and reprocess waste, so this is what they do, a descriptive definition.

clue.text: Ireland is besieged by diminutive female sheep

indicators.note: being besieged means being surrounded, so the Ireland word sits inside the female name

parts.note: Mo is a pet form of names such as Maureen
Erin is a poetic name for Ireland

explanation.surface: Ireland is surrounded by a small woman, oddly, ending in livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of sheep prized for its fine wool, an example of sheep.

clue.text: *Thumps heartless jerks

parts.note: the printed symbol is a star

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letters are removed, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone without feeling hits fools.
explanation.walkthrough: The star mark refers back to 1 Across; here it is simply read as a star.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden jumps or jolts are starts, as in waking with a start.

clue.text: Seriousness of actor Johnny's lisping

indicators.note: a lisp turns an s sound into th, so the actor's name is heard as a lisper would say it

parts.note: Johnny Depp is an American film actor

explanation.surface: A comment on how weighty the acting of Johnny Depp is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lisping' means Depp's said with a lisp, the final s heard as th.
explanation.definitionFit: Profundity or seriousness of thought, as in a writer of great depth, is a synonym.

clue.text: Vigorously administer a chest rub in Balkan city

indicators.note: giving a chest rub vigorously stirs the letters of the phrase into a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions for giving a hearty chest massage in a capital city of the Balkans.
explanation.definitionFit: Romania's capital lies in the Balkan region of south-east Europe, an example of a Balkan city.

clue.text: Pleasantly occupy morning with exercise

parts.note: am means morning, ante meridiem
to exercise a right is to use it

explanation.surface: Pass a morning agreeably with some exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain or divert someone is to keep them occupied in a pleasant way.

clue.text: Saw a lost paradise in Scandinavian country

indicators.note: lost means the letter a goes missing from the word saw

parts.note: Eden is the biblical paradise garden

explanation.surface: Someone saw a paradise lost, echoing Milton, in a Nordic land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lost' leaves SW from SAW; the surface echoes Milton's Paradise Lost.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the Scandinavian kingdoms, an example of a country in that region.

clue.text: Bra size that is transfixing Oregon resident

indicators.note: transfixing means piercing, so the state abbreviation is driven through by the other pieces

parts.note: OR is the US postal abbreviation for Oregon
a C cup is a bra size
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A woman of a certain bra size who lives in Oregon is staring at something.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lives in or holds a property is its occupant, a synonym for resident.

clue.text: Most reluctant, I agree to get into bed

indicators.note: to get into puts the agreeing word inside the bed word

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
yes is a way of saying I agree

explanation.surface: Someone shyly consents to going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of coy, meaning shy or reluctant, so most reluctant in the shy sense.

clue.text: Free intermingling of our genes

indicators.note: intermingling means the letters of the following words are mixed together

explanation.surface: A comment on the free mixing of two people's DNA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' looks like 'unrestricted', but here means giving freely, liberal.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal or open-handed with money or help, a synonym of free in the giving sense.
